summary: The prompt clearly states the goal (a Python LangChain agent that embeds correspondent profiles, stores vectors in Azure DocumentDB, searches sanctions/adverse-media, and returns a score, matches and a narrative). The provided skill.md supplies important run-time constraints (existing DocumentDB cluster, DB name, env var for connection string, index capabilities). Several implementation details are not specified (Python version, driver choice/version, embedding/chat model, exact data shapes, index parameters, API vs CLI, seed data). A builder can start, but will make several concrete assumptions (pymongo driver, OpenAI embeddings + chat models, FastAPI endpoint, typical embedding dimension such as 1536, collection names) unless the author clarifies them.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "embeds correspondent bank entity profiles, stores the vectors in DocumentDB, and searches against embedded sanctions list and adverse media entries on each review cycle"; "return a risk score, matched entries, and a plain-language risk narrative"
rubric.note: Functional goal and expected outputs are clearly stated.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use a modern Python 3.x runtime (assume Python 3.10 or 3.11) with a virtual environment; implement with pip/venv.
rubric.note: Language is given but no specific Python version is specified; skill.md only says python/pip resolve to a venv.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use the MongoDB-compatible Python driver pymongo, pinned to a current stable series compatible with MongoDB 7.0 (e.g. pymongo>=4.3,<5.0).
rubric.note: Prompt and skill.md do not name or pin a specific driver or version; builder will pick pymongo by convention.
skill.md supplies an existing vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster (compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol, DiskANN/HNSW/IVF support) and DOCUMENTDB_URI env var.
skill.md instructs the connection string is in DOCUMENTDB_URI and must not be written into files; use .env.example placeholders.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "embeds correspondent bank entity profiles"; "sanctions list and adverse media entries"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Create collections named 'correspondents', 'sanctions', and 'adverse_media' in database 'sample_banking_11'. Documents include fields: _id, name/title, metadata, embedding (vector as list/array), source, date, and any provenance fields.
rubric.note: Database name is provided by skill.md, but collection names and document shapes are not specified; builder will pick reasonable names/fields.

rubric.skill_that_covers: Run environment (skill.md) (asks to load sample data during verification)
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Include a small synthetic sample dataset (few correspondents, a few sanctions entries and adverse-media snippets) in repository (e.g. data/*.json) and provide a seed script to load it.
rubric.note: No data source, size, licence, nor concrete seed files are supplied; the builder must create synthetic samples.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "stores the vectors in DocumentDB, and searches against embedded sanctions list and adverse media entries"
rubric.skill_that_covers: Run environment (skill.md) (states cluster supports DiskANN, HNSW and IVF vector indexes and asks to create collections and indexes in verification)
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Create a cosmosSearch vector index (choose vector-hnsw by default) on the embedding field named 'embedding' with dimensions matching the embedding model (assume 1536 dims if using OpenAI text-embedding-3-small). Use $search / cosmosSearch vector query from the database for similarity search.
rubric.note: Index kind/type support is provided by skill.md, but index parameters and exact field names/dimensions are not specified.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use OpenAI embeddings (text-embedding-3-small, 1536 dims) via LangChain's embeddings interface, and use an OpenAI chat model (e.g., gpt-4o-mini or gpt-4o) via LangChain to generate the plain-language risk narrative. API keys come from environment variables (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY).
rubric.note: No embedding or chat model/provider is specified; this is a key implementation choice a builder will make.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Python LangChain agent" (no UI/CLI specified)
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Implement a small HTTP API (FastAPI) exposing a /search (or /review) endpoint that accepts a correspondent identifier or profile and returns JSON with risk_score, matches (with similarity scores), and risk_narrative.
rubric.note: Prompt does not specify CLI vs API vs UI; common sample pattern is an API route; reference requirements mention /search but the prompt did not.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Do not provision new DocumentDB clusters; use the provided cluster. The sample will not include cluster creation steps unless run policy permits writes.
rubric.note: skill.md explicitly discourages provisioning another cluster and instructs using the provided cluster.

rubric.skill_that_covers: Run environment (skill.md) (gives high-level verification steps but no concrete commands or unit test guidance)
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Provide a README with commands: pip install -r requirements.txt; export env vars per .env.example; python scripts/seed.py; uvicorn main:app; tests use pytest with mocking for DB and embedding calls.
rubric.note: Detailed run commands and unit test setup are not provided.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "The agent should return a risk score, matched entries, and a plain-language risk narrative for each correspondent reviewed."
rubric.note: Functional acceptance criteria are stated for the main feature.

rubric.skill_that_covers: Run environment (skill.md) (contains constraints like never write connection string, do not provision cluster)
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Keep dataset small to avoid large index choices and costs; do not attempt to provide production HA or infra-as-code for the real cluster.
rubric.note: Some constraints are in skill.md (secrets, no provisioning), but other constraints (cost limits, non-goals) are not specified.

rubric.skill_that_covers: Run environment (skill.md) (asks for .env.example and not to write real secrets; provides database name)
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Repository layout: README.md, src/ package, scripts/seed.py, requirements.txt (pinned), .env.example, tests/ with pytest, and a sample data/ directory.
rubric.note: skill.md suggests some conventions (.env.example, DB name) but not full conventions like pinned deps or exact layout.

contradictions: The starter prompt says "Using the DocumentDB skill", but the installed_skills list is empty; however a run-environment skill.md was supplied. Clarify whether the DocumentDB skill is available to the builder as an installed skill.
questions_for_author: Which embedding model and provider should be used (name and expected embedding dimension)?
Which chat / LLM model should generate the plain-language risk narrative (provider and model name)?
Which MongoDB-compatible Python driver and version should the sample use (e.g., pymongo and version pin)?
Should the sample expose an API (e.g., FastAPI /search endpoint), a CLI, or a simple script for the review cycle?
Do you want real sanctions/adverse media sample data or synthetic dummy data in the repository? Any preferred format or size?
requirements_at_risk: Embed correspondent bank entity profiles with a LangChain embeddings integration and store each profile's vector on its document in Azure DocumentDB using a MongoDB-compatible Python driver — not fully specified: builder must choose embedding provider/model and the Python MongoDB driver/version.

Create a cosmosSearch vector index (kind vector-ivf, vector-hnsw or vector-diskann) on the embedding field with dimensions matching the embedding model used — at risk: index kind/parameters and embedding dimensions are not specified.

On each review cycle, run vector similarity search inside Azure DocumentDB with $search / cosmosSearch using each correspondent's embedding — at risk: prompt does not explicitly require using $search/cosmosSearch syntax; builder may instead perform client-side nearest-neighbour filtering.
Derive a risk score for each correspondent from the similarity search results returned by Azure DocumentDB — at risk: method to derive the risk score (scaling/aggregation) is unspecified.

The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository — at risk: skill.md mandates DOCUMENTDB_URI env var but model credentials (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY) are not specified in prompt/skill.md.
A .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values — at risk: skill.md asks to use .env.example but does not enumerate all required env vars.
The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output — at risk: embedding model not specified so dimensions cannot be assuredly matched.
The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one — at risk: neither index parameters nor README guidance provided.
One database client is created and reused across requests — at risk: connection pooling/reuse is not specified in prompt or skill.md.
A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data — at risk: no seed files or idempotent seed script specified.
/search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails — at risk: error handling requirements are not in the prompt or skill.md.
Search results include the similarity score — at risk: prompt asks for matched entries but does not explicitly require including similarity scores in results.
Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt — at risk: pip environment is available but requirements pinning is not specified.
Unit tests run without a live cluster — at risk: no test strategy or mocking is specified for unit tests.
Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type — at risk: skill.md provides an existing cluster but no infra-as-code is included in prompt or skill.md.
The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up — at risk: README content requirements are not included in the prompt or skill.md.
The sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB" throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name — at risk: naming convention is not enforced in the prompt or skill.md.
